correctness.rationale: The primary paper establishes the Fraisse age and ultrahomogeneity of finite k-ary meet-trees and identifies finitely meet-generated closures with pairwise meets. The proof proves an exact bijection between unordered subset orbits and colored rooted trees with branching white vertices, obtains the cycle-index recurrence, proves sharp first arity separation by exhausting the n=k+1 branching possibilities, and establishes full overhead support and endpoint formulas from rooted-tree degree sums. verify.py independently checks literal lowest-common-ancestor closure, all bivariate coefficients for n<=6 and k<=6, first-difference identities, and known endpoint and OEIS controls; 740 assertions passed. No finite experiment is used in place of the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The natural orbit profile of explicitly known homogeneous k-ary meet-tree groups acquires a computable full bivariate rank refinement. The sharp minimal-arity witness identifies k at the first possible subset size with a coefficient-one obstruction; this is a structural group-action invariant beyond the known ungraded Greg count. Exact overhead support and two classical endpoint families provide a meaningful all-rank interpolation. Both the precise object and invariant are motivated independently of computation.
